scope: Proposition 10.5 (Status preparation) of the manuscript “A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-Colin-de-Verdiere-chromatic-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 157 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 97677c7a183884f0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 71-72. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants δ∗, c∗ > 0, fixed before the selector and channel sizes, with the following property. Along a subsequence, the original pooled unit law has a restriction of mass at least δ∗ whose first pin dimension is at most K1 and whose normalized leaves satisfy Equation (5.11). One of the following descriptions applies. (i) There is no prediction as in Theorem 10.1 on the first pooled law before the final negligible leaf trimming. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual small table is greater than .99. 71 (ii) A prediction with fixed αi, c and common classes ei is retained. Its marks and exceptions are preserved, and Equation (10.1) has uniform o(1) error on every retained unit. If both classes vanish, Equation (10.3) is exact on every unit. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual table satisfying Equation (10.8) is at least 1/64. In particular the corresponding successful pair event, measured in two draws from the original pooled law, has mass at least c∗. One may take δ∗ = 10−6δph 64 , c∗ = δ2 ∗ 64 , 0 < ηcol < c∗ 4 , (10.9) where 0 < δph ≤ 1 is the early retained-mass constant in Theorem 9.3. The colour bound in Equation (10.9) can be chosen using the initial M and early geometric constants only; the marginal constant L of the second distribution test does not enter it. After forgetting colour and other marks, the prepared law σ′ satisfies σ′ i ≤ M δ∗ π (i = 1, 2), σ′ ≤ 2(D+o(1))N P0 2 . (10.10) The endpoint primal marginals consequently have the same constant bound relative to pr∗ P0. Every normalized leaf has joint density at most 2O(N)P0 2 . The successful table event is detected by a finite list of numerical tables and separate unary orientation flags, together with leaf-pair tests. The size of this list is fixed in n, but need not be early.
